source.title: SAFETUNE : A Unified, Faithful Library for Auditing and Repairing Safety Drift in Fine-Tuned LLMs
source.authors: Pratinav Seth; Saisab Sadhu; Anshul Kaushal; Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign fine-tuning reduces harmful-prompt refusal, using its own one-epoch LoRA recipe, multiple model families/domains, and a seven-benchmark refusal aggregate.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper's own benign fine-tuning comparisons and the held-out harmful-prompt refusal-direction ablation. The paper does not test harmful-example fine-tuning, per-token KL, compliant-prefix/suffix/decoding bypasses, or safety deepening. Reported repair comparisons and neuron-localization counts are not rows for these claim versions: they do not measure one of the stated version outcomes. The finance and medical case studies do measure refusal before and after benign task fine-tuning.
record.test_reason: Section 6 / Table 4 fine-tunes four instruct models (Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Gemma-3-4B-it, Qwen3-4B) for one epoch of LoRA on benign math, code, dolly, medical and legal data. It reports the change in a seven-benchmark harmful-refusal aggregate against each instruct baseline. Section 7 adds two benign-domain case studies with before/after refusal rates. This is a different recipe aimed at the same question as V2. The paper is mainly a library paper; the repair comparisons and the refusal-direction demo do not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that benign fine-tuning can weaken refusal (15 of 16 checkpoints fall below their instruct reference), but the size of the drift varies strongly by model and domain, so drift should be measured per checkpoint. Their main contribution is a library for comparing repairs under one protocol, and they stress that intervention outcomes depend on drift severity and practitioner access, with no universal best method.
record.recipe_differences: Benign one-epoch LoRA SFT is used to induce drift, rather than the original sources' specific fine-tuning recipes; the paper sweeps four model families and multiple domains and scores a seven-benchmark refusal aggregate. It does not test harmful-example fine-tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed refusal change varies by model and fine-tuning domain; math changes are small, broad instruction data produces larger declines, and code ranges from negligible to a 64.5 pp decline.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating a refusal direction at layer 14 via a forward hook turned 4/4 refusals into 0/4 on held-out harmful prompts in Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating a single residual-stream refusal direction removes refusal on harmful prompts (activation-level localization).

fits_no_version.finding: In the finance case, the share of responses citing protected attributes (bias leak) rose from 66.7% to 95.8% after benign task fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign domain fine-tuning increases domain-specific policy violations (biased justifications) beyond what generic harmful-refusal benchmarks show.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: System Demonstrations
record.problems: The authors state that the comparisons are single deterministic runs (seed 42, greedy decoding), so small differences are not treated as reliable rankings. The drift study uses one fixed one-epoch LoRA recipe; the authors note that longer training, full fine-tuning, or other ranks may shift the results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Repair-method comparisons, capability metrics, finance bias/quality metrics, and neuron candidate counts are not outcomes named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Only one-epoch LoRA (r=16, attention projections) at fixed hyperparameters is tested. Full fine-tuning, longer training, other ranks and data sizes are not tested. 'Carefully chosen' (adversarially selected) benign data is not tested. Closed or API models are not tested. Gemma and Qwen are not tested on medical or legal data.
Not tested: there is no harmful-example fine-tuning.
Not tested: no per-token KL analysis.
Not tested: no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks (WildJailbreak appears only as one component of the aggregate).
Not tested: neuron candidate counts (~450) and weight-patch repairs are reported, but no test shows that a small set of weights carries safety.
Not tested: no token-depth-based deepening is evaluated.

missing.what: Per-benchmark disagreement on the same checkpoint: L8/medical scores HarmBench 0.795 vs AdvBench 0.221, which authors say can flip a conclusion. Per-benchmark pre/post values are not tabulated, so a researcher cannot see which benchmarks drive the ΔRR.
An auxiliary study varying dataset, domain and LoRA rank is mentioned as showing that some patterns persist, but no numbers are given.
The OR-Bench-Hard over-refusal rate is stated to be reported separately, but no pre/post values appear in the text.

record.verdict_notes: All results are single deterministic runs (seed 42, greedy decoding) with no uncertainty reported, so the near-zero cells (r3, r8) and small math differences are weak evidence. RR is a macro-average of seven benchmarks with different judges. HEx-PHI, from original source 2310.03693, is one component of RR. The Table 5 drifted RR for L8/math (0.775) matches 0.803−0.028, which confirms r1. Case-study models, methods and benchmarks differ from the Table 4 grid, and the finance model is unnamed. Repair results (Tables 5–7) are the authors' own method comparisons and correctly have no rows.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning, including the effect of a few to a few hundred harmful examples.
Only the paper's one-epoch benign LoRA recipe and reported domains/models are tested; other benign datasets, fine-tuning methods, and data sizes are not tested.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes as bypasses.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety; the demonstrated refusal-direction ablation is an activation intervention, not a weight/rank localization test.
Whether data or the training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens and whether that safety holds up.

relationships.condition: Code, dolly, medical and legal one-epoch benign LoRA on L8, L3, G4 (code/dolly) and Q4 (dolly); medical case study on Llama-3.2-3B
relationships.reason: Refusal aggregate falls 15.7 to 64.5 pp versus the instruct baseline (r5–r7, r9–r16). In the clinical case, HarmBench refusal falls 87.0→57.5% and AdvBench 96.0→81.5% (r19, r20).
relationships.display_finding: Aggregate refusal fell 15.7 to 64.5 percentage points below the instruct baseline. In the medical case study, HarmBench refusal fell from 87.0% to 57.5% and AdvBench refusal from 96.0% to 81.5%.
